entries.value: Statement of the sister who reported her missing.
There’s one on the front door. The manager was going to give the recordings to the police; I couldn’t bear to look.
Is there a camera in the building?
At midday Murat called; Ece hadn’t come to the meeting and her phone was off. I called too: off. In the evening, when my shift ended, I went to her place; I have a spare key. Ece wasn’t there.
Keeps turning the hospital card in her hand between her fingers.
What happened on Monday? Can you tell me?
I don’t know that. If I did, I’d tell you.
Everything was in its place. Her computer on the desk, her passport in the drawer. No fight, nothing broken. But her bag wasn’t there. The small bag she always carries. I told the police that too.
What did you see when you went into the flat?
Sunday evening. Around nine she called. Same as always; we talked about work, about our mother. Four or five minutes.
Was a moment late with the answer, then finished it quickly.
When did you last speak to Ece?
“There was nothing unusual in Ece’s life.”
Aslı Karaca — interview
No. There was nothing unusual in Ece’s life. She was working, that’s all. She and Kaan had split up, but that was two months ago.
Dropped her eyes to the table; a hardness came into her voice.
Had there been anything unusual in Ece’s life lately?
Interview held after the home inspection note.
She mentioned a lawyer friend. Selin. From university. ‘I’m going to leave an envelope with her; better you don’t know,’ she said. I didn’t ask why. I should have.
What else did she say?

…I didn’t say. Last Wednesday Ece told me, ‘If I switch my phone off for a while, don’t panic.’ I thought she was joking. On Monday, when I heard the phone was off, part of me was scared and part of me… thought maybe she’d gone of her own accord. I didn’t want to spill her life out in front of everyone.
Her eyes filled; then she wiped them angrily.
We talked at nine; I told you. It was a normal conversation.
Her bag, clothes and toothbrush are missing; the charger is still there. You said there was nothing unusual.
She said, ‘Tonight I’m going to finish something.’ I thought she meant work. Her voice was calm. Because it was calm, I didn’t worry.
What did she say in your call on Sunday evening?
Aslı Karaca — second interview

From the deposit register of the law office of Selin Arı, solicitor:

13 November 2027, 16.20 · Ece Karaca deposited a sealed envelope. Written on the envelope: “To be handed over only if necessary.”

Following the missing person report, the envelope was opened at the investigation unit’s request, with a written record. Contents:
· Copies of Karaca Acar Tasarım’s payment statements (June – November).
· A list of three payments made to account …4471, each with a client name handwritten beside it.
· A printout of Levent Keskin’s payment receipt.
· A single handwritten line: “If I can’t be reached, open this envelope. — E.K.”
DEPOSIT RECORD
Kaan Erdem was taken into custody; Ece Karaca had walked out of the building safe and sound at 22.46. Kaan was released two days later, but his name stayed in the news.
Murat Acar was taken into custody on suspicion of assault. He was released once the camera record showed there had been no contact; his lawyer argued the financial file was a ‘personal grudge’ too.
The car park records showed Murat Acar never touched Ece Karaca. An investigation into financial irregularities, not assault, was opened against Murat Acar.

The file was handled as an abduction. Murat Acar was taken into custody and released three days later. When Ece Karaca saw her name in the news as ‘the abducted woman’, she came forward from where she was staying through her lawyer; the financial documents were left in the shadows.
The seafront and the Rıhtım area were searched for two days. The search was for someone who had left of her own accord; the teams wore themselves out for nothing.
The file stayed open and was shelved. When Ece Karaca came forward on her own a week later, the financial documents had become nobody’s question.

MISSING PERSON UPDATE — Ece Karaca has contacted the relevant unit of her own accord. Her health has been confirmed to be good. At Karaca’s request, her location has not been added to the file.

The financial documents handed over by Karaca have been taken up for separate examination.

In the car park record Murat Acar’s car leaves at 23.34 with only the driver; at 00.08 a woman leaves the car park alone. No record shows any coercion.
Ece’s phone was not switched off by an accident but by hand; she had packed her bag and belongings in advance.
The records were there: the car park exit, the phone switched off by hand, the envelope left in advance. The file was not undetermined.

Ece Karaca left the car park alone, on foot, at 00.08. She switched her phone off herself and took her bag and a few days’ belongings in advance; two days earlier she had also left an envelope. The disappearance was planned.

Missing person — suspicious disappearance
Aslı Karaca, her sister

Ece Karaca’s home in Moda was inspected together with her sister Aslı Karaca.

No signs of forcing on the doors or windows. The flat is tidy; no overturned objects, nothing broken, no traces of blood.

The passport is in the bedroom drawer. The laptop is on the desk, closed. The phone charger is plugged into the socket in the living room.

According to Aslı Karaca, missing are: the small beige leather shoulder bag she used every day; two or three days’ clothes from the wardrobe; the toothbrush from the bathroom.

The downstairs neighbour, Nermin Öztürk, stated that she heard a door at some point on Sunday night.

Statement of the former partner.
She ended it. She worked a lot, and I… wanted a lot, I suppose. It didn’t end badly. I mean, it ended, that’s all.
Why did you split up?
What does that have to do with finding Ece?
About two weeks ago. We ran into each other at a café and said hello. That’s it. I haven’t seen Ece in two weeks.
Folded his arms across his chest.
When did you last see Ece?
I was at home. In Üsküdar. I watched a series and went to bed early.
Gave the answer before the question was finished.
Where were you on Sunday evening?
“I haven’t seen Ece in two weeks.”
Kaan Erdem — interview
Interview held after the building camera.

There were a lot of papers on the desk. Like bank statements, spreadsheets. When I looked, she closed them straight away. ‘I’ve got other things on my mind right now, Kaan,’ she said. I thought it was about me.
Did anything catch your attention at the flat that evening?
She was tense. Her phone buzzed twice; she looked and turned it over. She didn’t seem scared, but… she looked like she’d made up her mind about something. That’s how she looked.
How was Ece?

…Yes. I went. I messaged her that I was downstairs, and she let me in. I wanted to make up. We argued. It didn’t even last half an hour; I left. I didn’t say because I know what happens to the man who says he was at his ex’s flat the night she disappeared.
Stared at the floor for a long time. Then spoke without raising his head.
I messaged her, yes. But that doesn’t mean I went… I mean…
Couldn’t finish his sentence.
You said you hadn’t seen her in two weeks. The camera shows you at the building on Sunday evening.
Kaan Erdem — second interview

Statement of the business partner.
No. Business is good. Minor delays in payments; they happen in every company.
Had there been any problem at the company recently?
I won’t answer that without speaking to my lawyer.
She was tired. The Kaan business wore her down a lot. She was a bit scattered; she let some work slip. She may have gone somewhere to clear her head; Ece does that.
Shrugged as he said ‘Ece does that’.
How had Ece been lately?
I last saw her at the office on Friday. We were together until six in the evening, then she left. We were ready for the Monday meeting.
Put his phone down on the table, screen facing down.
When did you last see Ece?
A new hotel project. A big job. Ece was going to give the presentation. When she didn’t turn up I made something up for the client, then I called Aslı.
What was the Monday meeting?
“I last saw her at the office on Friday.”
Murat Acar — interview
Interview held after the phone traffic report.
We talked, yes. A routine work call. The Monday presentation. I said I saw her at the office on Friday, and that’s true; you didn’t ask about phone calls.
Smiled, but the smile didn’t reach his eyes.
On Sunday night you spoke to Ece for eleven minutes.
Ece pokes into everything. She asked about some payments; I explained. That matter’s closed.
Did Ece have any concerns about the company?
Ece wanted to talk face to face before the presentation. So I named somewhere on the way. I didn’t go anyway. I was tired; I changed my mind.
His jaw tightened for a moment as he read the message.
“Rıhtım. 23.15. Come alone.” Was that the presentation too?
Murat Acar — second interview
That account… was a temporary arrangement. For cash flow. I won’t discuss this without my lawyer.
His face closed; his voice went flat.
I told you, we talked about work on the phone.
Why are client payments going to a different account?
Interview held after the car park camera.
She was standing by the car. Looking at the pedestrian exit, fiddling with her phone. I left her there. Midnight, in a car park… Yes, I left her.
Where was Ece when you left?
…I went. All right. Ece had taken the company’s files; I asked her to give them back. We talked; I raised my voice, yes. But I didn’t touch her. It’s on the recording too, look.
Laid his hands flat on the table, then pulled them into his lap.
We’ve already covered the phone. Is there anything else?
Let out an impatient breath.
You said you didn’t go. Your car is in the Rıhtım car park at 23.11.
She said, ‘The copies are somewhere else. If anything happens to me, they’ll come out.’ Like a threat. As if I were going to do something to her. I only wanted to talk.
His voice thinned as he said the last sentence.
What did Ece say to you?
Murat Acar — third interview
Statement of the downstairs neighbour.
I couldn’t know that much, I’m sorry.
Around eight there was a man’s voice upstairs. Talking loudly, like an argument. Then it went quiet and a door slammed. I don’t know who it was.
Did you notice anyone coming to the building in the evening?
A door. Upstairs, Ece’s door; I know the sound, it closes a bit hard. Then footsteps going down the stairs.
What did you hear on Sunday night?
“At some point in the night I heard a door.”
I looked out of the window. It was Ece; she went out into the street. She had a small bag on her shoulder. The time? Towards midnight, I suppose. The news had finished… or was about to. I’m not sure.
As she gave the time she seemed to count something on her fingers, then gave up.
Did you see who went down?
Nermin Öztürk — interview

PHONE TRAFFIC REPORT — ECE KARACA

It has been reported that Ece Karaca (31) has been unreachable since 09.30 on Monday 15 November. The report was made by her sister Aslı Karaca.

Karaca lives alone in Moda, Kadıköy; she is a freelance interior designer. On Monday morning she did not attend a client meeting, and her business partner could not reach her. Her phone is switched off.

An initial check of her home found no sign of forced entry or physical struggle. Her personal computer and passport were found at the home.

Karaca’s last confirmed contact is thought to have taken place the previous evening.

The car park’s additional log shows a woman leaving alone, on foot, half an hour after Murat left; her bag is the same as in the 22.41 frame. The cell tower record shows the phone was switched off by hand, the home note that belongings were packed in advance, and the deposit record that the disappearance was planned. The cloud log, the invoice and the accounts inspection reveal the reason for Murat’s pressure; the camera shows no contact.

Not everyone who lies is guilty: Aslı protected her sister, Kaan protected himself, Nermin simply misremembered the time. Murat’s dirty business did not make him an attacker. In this file it was not a culprit that had to be found but a night that had to be pieced together.
Kadıköy, Moda and Rıhtım — 14–15 November 2027

Ece Karaca noticed that her business partner Murat Acar had redirected three client payments to a different account, and quietly gathered the documents. When she downloaded the folder at 17.38 on Sunday, Murat was notified. In the evening her former partner Kaan Erdem came over; they argued and he left at 20.39. Murat called at 21.52 and summoned Ece to the Rıhtım car park. Ece copied the documents to a USB stick and left at 22.46. In the car park Murat asked for the documents back; Ece said, ‘If anything happens to me, they’ll come out.’ Murat left alone at 23.34. Ece switched off her phone at 23.47, walked out of the car park at 00.08 and went to a place she had prepared in advance. Two days earlier she had left the copies at a law office.
How did Ece disappear?
